reuse.why: Adds getExpectedScheduleAmount beside the existing getScheduledAmount in the same module instead of changing it, so the client paths that use getScheduledAmount keep the old midpoint rule.

duplication.why: The new helper repeats getScheduledAmount's null/number/range dispatch under another name, and the midpoint copies in forecast-schedules.ts and schedule-template.ts are left in place.

placement.why: The helper sits in shared/schedules.ts and the API field is computed in scheduleModel.toExternal in api-models.ts, the layers where that logic belongs.

scope.why: Only the amount rule, the API field and tests.

maintainability.why: Two competing definitions of a schedule's expected amount now disagree (getScheduledAmount and the untouched forecast/template sites still average), so a future rule change has several places to find.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount in shared/schedules.ts goes around the existing getScheduledAmount; forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule and budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList keep their own midpoint expressions.

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount re-expresses getScheduledAmount's missing/number/range dispatch under a new name with an op parameter instead of extending the existing helper.

abstraction_drift.where: The new shared helper gained an op parameter for approximate amounts; getScheduledAmount (used by the desktop client), forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule and budget/schedule-template.ts still compute the amount themselves with the old midpoint rule.
